thread:
Alex: FYI p99 spiked ~11:42 in us-west, investigating. I opened a tiny hotfix PR that reverts a recent connpool tweak — need one more pair of eyes before I merge and roll forward. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2198 :eyes:
Jordan: Can you paste the diff or the exact change?
Alex: It's a one-line change in connpool.go, fallback to single-conn when backoff hits threshold. Diff:
```diff
- maxConns = 64
+ maxConns = 1 // temp fallback for p99 regressions
```
Alex: Ran a 5% canary after pushing the branch, latency looked back to baseline on that split. No errors flagged in logs there.
Maria: I'll take a quick look, giving it ~10–15m. Any reason we can't ship this immediately if canary is clean?
Alex: Mainly want to avoid surprising full-throughput behavior. This reduces concurrency so throughput drops slightly, but it's safer than continued p99 regressions.
Sam: @Maria if you approve I can merge and kick a rolling deploy within the next maintenance window (if we want immediate, I can do a fast roll). :thumbsup:
Trina: Quick ask — can we add a short TODO comment linking to the incident and an issue to re-evaluate the connpool heuristic? Prevents this being a permanent bandaid.
Alex: Good call. I'll add a TODO and an issue after merge.
Jordan: lgtm from me on the change itself. Verified no other callers rely on maxConns being >1 in that codepath.
Maria: Approved, left a tiny nit about log text. Not blocking.
Sam: Merging now and starting a 10-min canary at 20% traffic. Will watch p99 and errors.
deploy-bot: Deployment started: runtime/hotfix/connpool-fallback -> canary (20%). Track: https://deploys.redwood.dev/deploys/7981
Alex: Thanks all — I’ll follow up with the incident thread and open the follow-up issue.
Sam: Canary looks stable at +15m, p99 back to normal. Rolling to 100% now.
Alex: Roll complete. Marking incident resolved for now, will file postmortem notes later. :white_check_mark:
Trina: Thanks everyone!
